chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Fadhl from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: In the case of a man who freed his slave while death was approaching him, and he bore witness to that, and the slave's value was six hundred dirhams, and he had a debt of three hundred dirhams, and he left nothing else, he said: 'One-sixth of him is freed, because he only has three hundred, and he has one-sixth of the total.'
ai.seo_question: How is a slave's emancipation valued and settled against debts when a master dies near death?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the legal principle of *'itq* (manumission) is applied to an estate with limited liquidity, demonstrating how the value of the slave is treated as a debt to be paid from the deceased's assets. The ruling prioritizes the settlement of existing debts before allocating the one-sixth share for emancipation, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on balancing creditor rights with the spiritual merit of freeing a believer. This specific calculation underscores the practical application of estate distribution rules in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* when assets are insufficient to cover all obligations in full.
